messages.subject: extended.pgls and trajectory.analysis
messages.body_plain:
Dear geomorph community,

I am working on a phylogenetic control requested by reviewers, and I would like to know whether extended.pgls() can be combined with trajectory.analysis().

My data and design
- Multivariate shape data (48 variables) for 195 individuals of 6 species, with many individuals per species.
- Species = species (factor); Stage = an ordered three-level factor (e.g., low, medium and high wear: S1, S2, S3). The goal is to build one trajectory per species, with the three stages as trajectory points, and to compare trajectories among species (length, direction, shape).
- Phylogeny: a pruned cladogram with branch lengths assigned (Grafen), with tips matching the levels of Species.

What I did

Ordinary model (works as expected):

fit_ordinary <- procD.lm(Y ~ Species * Stage, data = my_data, iter = 999)
TA_ordinary <- trajectory.analysis(fit_ordinary, groups = my_data$Species,
                                   traj.pts = my_data$Stage, pca = TRUE)

Here the trajectory points are exactly equal to the species-by-stage means of the individual scores in the PC space returned by plot(TA_ordinary).

Phylogenetic model:

fit_phylo <- extended.pgls(Y ~ Species * Stage, data = my_data,
                           species = "Species", phy = my_tree, iter = 999)
TA_phylo <- trajectory.analysis(fit_phylo, groups = my_data$Species,
                                traj.pts = my_data$Stage, pca = TRUE)

trajectory.analysis() runs without errors, but the trajectory points do not match the data. For example, for one species (Species_A), comparing the mean of the individual scores in each stage with the trajectory point, both in the PC space of TA_phylo:

          mean of individuals       trajectory point
          PC1       PC2             PC1       PC2
S1       -0.257     0.060          -2.609     0.061
S2       -0.141     0.030          -1.802    -0.431
S3        0.249     0.134           2.423     0.585

My questions
1. Is trajectory.analysis() intended to work with objects of class lm.rrpp.ws <http://lm.rrpp.ws> returned by extended.pgls()? If not, is there a recommended way to run a trajectory analysis conditioned on the phylogeny when each trajectory corresponds to a different species?
2. Is there any  limitation when the groups used for the trajectories (Species) are also the species used in the phylogenetic covariance structure?

Some cells are small (for example, n = 2 individuals in a few species-by-stage combinations), in case this is relevant.

I can provide a reproducible example or share the data  if that would help.

Thank you very much for your time.

Best regards,
Ale

geomorph_4.1.1
RRPP_2.2.0

messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] extended.pgls and trajectory.analysis
messages.body_plain:
Ale,

Yes, trajectory.analysis can work with extended.pgls/lm.rrpp.ws <http://lm.rrpp.ws>.  In our 2024 paper where we introduced extended PGLS, we did precisely that in the pupfish example: extended PGLS + TA.

However, I can replicate the shift in group means in the plot that you described, so a bug seems to have been introduced somewhere.

We will investigate that.

Dean

messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] extended.pgls and trajectory.analysis
messages.body_plain:
Dear Ale, and everyone,

The issue was caused by a missing phylogenetic transformation of the model matrix used to obtain least-squares means in the RRPP::pairwise function, used within trajectory.analysis (not extended.pgls).  I am hopeful this would cause no major issues with the trajectory analysis, itself, but just the resulting graph.  Phylogenetic transformations were used to obtain random pseudo-data via RRPP and the model matrix for LS means was constructed properly, but not having the phylogenetic transformation in the last step meant the LS means were shifted away from the origin in the PC plot.  This would be a consistent (affine) shift in each RRPP permutation.

Please re-install RRPP from my Gtihub (mlcollyer/RRPP) and see if your results make sense.  Let me know if issues persist.  I will soon send an update to CRAN, but wish to test the function more first.

Sorry for the bug!

Mike
